what: The weighted second route's numbers (docs/decisions.md addendum 11), encoding docs/research/acceptance-rule-review.md, section 'The proposed rule', as committed in 24e106b. Changes only by an addendum. Read by tools/accept_weighted.py, which tools/climb_accept.py prints beside its verdict.
unit: night points: points of one 8-max table on the 8..1 table (F scores about 6.0 there against night)

units.what: factor taking a cell's own points to night points. A heads-up or three-handed rules file sets the factor; the top_heavy variant sets it next; else the cell's payout table (the label's ' @' part, 8..1 when absent)

why.8..1: the night cell's own table (night, guards, elite stage, variants, aware)
why.10/7/5/4/3/2/1/0: ratio of spreads, 7/10 (night @brief, the 8-max exploit cells)
why.hu: heads-up 10/7: the night has no heads-up tables; heads-up decides 8 against 7 on an 8..1 table

adapters.name: adapters
adapters.rule: 8-max, three-handed and heads-up a third each; inside a format each adapter bot a fixed quarter; a bot not run counts 0 +- 0

twist_realistic.name: twist, twist-blind field
twist_realistic.rule: the catalogued variants on realistic, each by its probability below, renormalised over the variants with a cell

twist_aware.name: twist, twist-aware field
twist_aware.rule: the aware cells, each twist by its probability below, renormalised over the twists with a cell; cells on the same twist split it

variant_probability.source: docs/drills/climb/variants-ranked.md, column P (percent); only ratios matter

interval: family block: a family's half-width is the share-weighted sum of its cells' unit-converted half-widths (perfect correlation inside the family); families combine as independent (the square root of the sum of (weight x half-width) squared). The lower bound is the weighted mean minus that interval.
w_min: the same lower bound with each family's weight anywhere in its plausible range, summing to 1, set least favourably to the candidate: the minimum over the corners of the ranges (the bound is concave in the weights, so the minimum sits at a corner)

cap.test: a cell breaks the cap when its unit-converted upper bound, factor x (delta + ci), is below -0.03 night points
cap.own_points_note: the same cap in each scale's own points, 0.03 divided by the factor and rounded as addendum 11 prints it; the test uses the night-point form

missing.identical_by_construction: a cell documented as identical by construction counts as 0 +- 0 (climb_accept --identical): 'holdem' for a change that plays only twist tables (the ordinary room, strong tables and adapters count 0 +- 0 where not run), 'twists' for a change gated to hold'em tables (the 22 variants not in holdem_tables), or one variant's name. A twist claimed identical with no cell gets a 0 +- 0 cell in both twist families.
missing.inside_a_family: the cells that ran share the family's weight (shares renormalised over them); adapters are the exception, with fixed per-bot shares (a bot not run counts 0 +- 0)
missing.family_not_run: dropped and the others reweighted (and, for W-min, the ranges scaled by the present families' base weights when they cannot sum to 1). Allowed on a screen, never under route 2.

conditions: the main rule rejects the candidate
a fresh held-out set (H<k>) with every stage run, the full catalogue at 200 seeds or more, the protocol's own cells (no --rules, --variant or --variants)
(a) the W-min family-block lower bound is above zero
(c) no judge beyond noise down (the judges stage on the judge set, once per batch)
(d) each down cell is written up in the log with its cause

notes: top is a guards-stage cell but the section puts it in the strong-table family (share 0.15); climb_accept's family follows the field, not the stage.

elite_b and mirror_b (the second elite wave, after most reviewed verdicts) are in the strong-table family at the section's 0.20 and 0.10. On a verdict without them the strong cells that ran share the family.

exploit3, exploit3_hu and exploit3_3 are exploiter 3's cells, adapt, adapt_hu and adapt_3 are adapt1's (R6's tuning copy, addendum 9): both bots are among the section's four adapter bots, each a fixed quarter of every format.
The adapters' 8-max cells are played at 10/7/5/4/3/2/1/0 (factor 0.7), heads-up at 10/7 (1/3), three-handed at 10/7/5 (0.4), as the section's units table says.
The judge cells (the list above) carry no weight: route 2's condition (c) reads them. adapt_judge* are adapt2's cells, the held-out copy (addendum 9), so they are judges, not adapters.

Aware cells beyond the four hand-built fields (generic_aware under any variant, FIELD:VARIANT cells such as realistic_keep2:deal5_keep2) are in the twist-aware family under their variant, by the section's principle: the aware cells by the probability of their twist, cells on the same twist splitting it.
A variant that variants-ranked.md does not list (a variant file, a new catalogue entry) gets probability 1, the smallest listed row and the review script's default.

A hold'em cell whose label the section does not list (a cell under a --rules file, a new guard) goes to its field's family at share 0.05, the review script's default for an unnamed cell; its factor follows its label's payout table. A cell whose field is in no family is reported as not weighted.
The window stage is not weighted: it is its own check (prompt 06). Cells under --rules or --variant are the night's game, not the protocol's, so the block warns and route 2 refuses them.
The twist half never drops below 0.25 under W-min: that follows from the ranges' lower bounds (0.10 + 0.15) and needs no extra constraint.
The cap is tested on every weighted cell, measured or identical (an identical cell is 0 +- 0 and never breaks it), never on judges.
The section says to use the exact per-seed interval once climb_accept computes it; addendum 11 fixed the family-block interval, which is what this file and climb_accept use.
